title: Mandatory: long-term disability insurance
summary: No employer means no group disability coverage. The single most important insurance for working-age contractors.
detailsHtml:
Why this is non-negotiable

A W-2 employee usually has at least basic short-term disability through their employer. A contractor has nothing. For someone whose income depends entirely on their ability to work, a disabling injury or illness is an extinction-level financial event without insurance. Long-term disability premiums run 1–3% of income — high relative to other insurance, low relative to what they protect.

Own-occupation coverage

The critical clause for skilled contractors is "own-occupation" coverage — meaning benefits pay if you can't perform your specific occupation, not just any occupation. A surgeon who can answer phones at a call center is not disabled under "any-occupation" definitions but is clearly disabled in any meaningful sense. Own-occupation is more expensive but worth the difference for specialized professionals.
